title: Implement stereo processor with pan width lf mono and correlation
description:
Create Source/DSP/StereoProcessor.h and Source/DSP/StereoProcessor.cpp implementing wet-path stereo placement, width, low-frequency mono, and correlation telemetry for ShredSpace.

Before editing, inspect:
- Source/DSP/DelayVoice.h and Source/DSP/DelayVoice.cpp and, if present, Source/DSP/RoutingEngine.h (to see how wet channels are produced and where stereo shaping is applied)
- Any existing Source/DSP/*.h module and match its namespace, pragma-once/header-guard style, include style, and naming conventions exactly
- CMakeLists.txt (C++20 standard, JUCE modules available) but do not edit it

Required behavior (implement exactly these equations):
1. Constant-power pan for p in [-1, 1]: gain_L = cos(pi*(p+1)/4), gain_R = sin(pi*(p+1)/4). Clamp p to [-1, 1].
2. Mid/side width for w in [0, 2]: M = (L + R)/sqrt(2), S = (L - R)/sqrt(2), L_out = (M + w*S)/sqrt(2), R_out = (M - w*S)/sqrt(2). At w = 1 this is an exact identity round-trip (L_out == L, R_out == R within floating-point tolerance). Clamp w to [0, 2].
3. Low-frequency mono: split each wet channel at a crossover frequency in the range 60-500 Hz, default 180 Hz. Form M_low = (L_low + R_low)/2 and output M_low summed with each channel's high band, so content below the crossover collapses to mono while content above it retains its stereo image. Use a complementary first-order or Linkwitz-Riley style split built from JUCE DSP filters already available in the project; do not introduce a new dependency. The dry path is unaffected: this class operates on wet channels only.
4. Correlation telemetry: accumulate smoothed sumLR, sumL2, sumR2 and compute correlation = sumLR / sqrt(sumL2*sumR2 + epsilon), clamped to [-1, 1]. Publish it as a scalar via std::atomic<float> for display only; never construct strings or touch GUI objects from the audio thread.

API shape: a class StereoProcessor with prepare(double sampleRate, int maxBlockSize), reset(), setPan(float p), setWidth(float w), setLowFrequencyMonoCrossover(float hz), setLowFrequencyMonoEnabled(bool), a stereo block process function, and getCorrelation() returning the atomic telemetry value.

Smoothing by domain (binding): pan uses linear juce::SmoothedValue at 30 ms; width uses linear juce::SmoothedValue at 50 ms; the crossover frequency is strictly positive and uses multiplicative smoothing at 50 ms. Real-time rules: no heap allocation, locks, file IO, string construction, GUI calls, unbounded loops, or buffer resizing in the process path; all filter state and scratch storage allocated in prepare sized for the maximum block size.

Do not modify DelayVoice, CMakeLists.txt, or any other file; integration and build registration happen in task e.5. No artist or song names may appear anywhere in the source.
acceptance_criteria: Source/DSP/StereoProcessor.h and Source/DSP/StereoProcessor.cpp exist and declare/define a StereoProcessor class with prepare, reset, setPan, setWidth, crossover setters, a stereo process function, and getCorrelation
StereoProcessor.cpp implements constant-power pan gain_L = cos(pi*(p+1)/4) and gain_R = sin(pi*(p+1)/4) with p clamped to [-1,1]

StereoProcessor.cpp implements M=(L+R)/sqrt(2), S=(L-R)/sqrt(2), L_out=(M+w*S)/sqrt(2), R_out=(M-w*S)/sqrt(2) with w clamped to [0,2], and the w=1 case reproduces the input exactly within floating-point tolerance
Low-frequency mono splits each wet channel at a crossover clamped to [60, 500] Hz defaulting to 180 Hz, sums M_low=(L_low+R_low)/2 with the high bands, and leaves the dry path untouched
Correlation telemetry is computed as sumLR/sqrt(sumL2*sumR2 + epsilon), clamped to [-1,1], and published through a std::atomic<float>
Pan smooths linearly over 30 ms, width smooths linearly over 50 ms, and the crossover frequency uses multiplicative smoothing over 50 ms
No heap allocation, locking, file IO, or string construction occurs in StereoProcessor process-path functions; all state is allocated in prepare
No file outside the task's allowed_write_paths is created or modified
forbidden_changes: modify Source/DSP/ModulationEngine.h, Source/DSP/ModulationEngine.cpp, Source/DSP/SoftSaturator.h, Source/DSP/SoftSaturator.cpp, Source/DSP/ShortDiffuser.h, or Source/DSP/ShortDiffuser.cpp
apply width, pan, or low-frequency mono to the dry signal path
use multiplicative smoothing for pan or width, or linear smoothing for the crossover frequency
publish correlation telemetry through strings, shared_ptr, or GUI objects from the audio thread
allocate memory, lock, construct strings, or perform file IO inside process-path functions
include artist or song names in source or comments
